raw_segments.text: He said, and we with glad consent obey, forsake the seat, and leaving few behind, we spread
our sails before the willing wind.
Now from the sight of land our galleys move, with only seas around and skies above.
When o'er our heads descends a burst of rain, and night with sable clouds involves the main.
The ruffling winds the foamy billows' rays.
The scattered fleet is forked to several ways.
The face of heathen is ravished from our eyes, and in redoubled peals the roaring thunder
flies.
Cast from our course, we wander in the dark.
No stars to guide, no point of land to mark.
Even palinuris no distinction found betwixt the night and day, such darkness reigned around.
Three starless nights the doubtful navy strays without distinction, and three sunless days.
The fourth renews the light, and from our shrouds we view a rising land, like distant
clouds.
The mountaintops confirm the pleasing sight, and curling smoke ascending from their height.
The canvas falls, their oars the sailors ply, from the rude strokes the whirling waters
fly.
At length I land upon the strawfades, safe from the danger of the stormy seas.
Those isles are compassed by T.H.
Yeonian mane, the dire abode where the foul harpies reign, forked by the winged warriors
to repair to their old homes, and leave their costly fare.
Monsters more fierce offended heave and ne'er sent from hell's abyss, for human punishment,
with virgin faces, but with wombs obscene, foul ponches, and with order still unclean,
with claws for hands, and looks for ever lien.
